newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says will not raise taxes as part of reform.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says will not raise taxes as part of reform.

text.p: Mexico will not raise taxes but instead try to broaden the tax base as part of an upcoming tax reform, Finance Ministry spokesman Alejandro Valenzuela said on Wednesday.
He told a news conference that talks on tax reform between the government and business representatives would begin this week.
"We will not raise taxes. Taxes will remain the same," Valenzuela told reporters.
He said officials will try to simplify taxes and also increase the tax base. A small minority of Mexicans actually pay taxes, according to official statistics.
"On the federal level...we need to help meet spending needs without raising debt levels or hurting our inflation goals -- that is, keeping public finances healthy," he said.
Valenzuela said the government's new Pronafide economic program outlines the possibility of tax breaks for reinvestment of corporate profits and job-creating investment.
Valenzuela added Mexico's markets have been very steady ahead of upcoming mid-term elections on July 6.

"The data for the second quarter ... looks encouraging both in public finances and industrial production which leads us to predict vigorous growth for the second quarter and the rest of the year," he said.
